 Judgment

Parents of deceased Dhanranesh filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of Canter bearing No.AP-39-W-6438 asserting that on 08.01.2022 at about 05.00 AM when Dhanranesh and others are standing beside car No.AP-09-BG-9749 which was in stationary between Reddygollahalli Cross and Doddapayalagurki cross, (NH-44) within the limits of Peresandra Police Station,
Chikkaballapura District
, driver of Canter bearing No.AP-39-W-6438 drove the same negligently dashed the same to Dharanesh and car No.AP- 09-BG-9749, thereby caused accident caused death of Dhanranesh.
2. As on the date of the accident Dhanranesh being aged about 22 years use to earn Rs.20,000/- per month by working as Coolie.
3. Regarding the accident Peresandra Police registered a case in Crime No.01/2022 for the offence punishable under Sec. 279, 337 & 304(A) IPC against driver of Canter.

4. In response to the notice, the respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through his Advocate and filed written statement denying the allegations regarding the reason and mode of the accident, age, occupation and income of deceased Dhanranesh.
5. Inspite of service of notice, respondent No.1 remained absent.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 07.03.2023, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, on 08.01.2022 at about 5.00 a.m to 5.15 a.m,
on NH-44, Bengaluru-Hyderabad Road

, In between Reddygollahalli Cross and Doddapayalagurki Cross of Chikkaballapura taluk, the death caused to one C.
Dharanish @ Dharanesh C., was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the driver of the Itcher Canter vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP-39-W-6438 as alleged?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?

7. On 05.6.2023, 14.6.2023, 20.6.2023, petitioner No.1 deposed as PW1, produced 14 documents at Exhibits P.1 to P.14.
8.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the contesting parties and perused the records.

2

9. On the basis of the material available in the file, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ...

Petitioners are entitled to receive Rs.25,51,000/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. from the respondents,
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence affidavit PW1 mother of Dhanranesh stated that on 08.01.2022 at about 05.00 AM when Dhanranesh and others are standing beside stationary car No.AP-09-BG-9749 between Reddygollahalli Cross and Doddapayalagurki Cross, NH-44 within the limits of Peresandra Police Station, Gudibande Taluk, Chikkaballapura District driver of the Canter bearing No. AP-39-W-6438 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to Dharanesh and car No.AP-09-BG-9749 thereby caused the accident, caused death of Dhanranesh.
11.
In the written statement respondent No.2 insurance company denied the allegation regarding the reason and mode of the accident.
12. In the cross-examination, PW1 submitted that herself and her husband never witnessed the accident.

13. Ex.P.1 & P.2 are the copy of FIR and complaint pertaining to crime No.01/2022 registered by Peresandra Police against driver of Canter bearing No.AP-39-W-6438 for having committed the offences punishable under Section 279 and 304(A) of IPC., regarding the accident taken place on 08.01.2022 at 05.15 AM on Bengaluru- Hyderabad NH-44 between Reddygollahalli cross and Doddapayalagurki cross where Dhanranesh and others who are standing beside stationary car No.
AP-39-W-6438 resulting in the death of Dharanesh on the basis of the complaint filed by Narasingaraju S/o Narayanappa.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of the spot mahazar.
Ex.P4 is the copy of the sketch of the place of accident.

Ex.P.5 is the copy of the chargesheet filed by Peresandra Police in Crime No. 01/2022 against Srinivasachari A.V.S/o Venkatachari driver of Canter No.
AP-39-W-6438 for having committed the offence punishable under Section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.,
Ex.P5 is the PM Report pertaining to the body of Dharanesh.
14. Ex.P6 is the copy of the Inquest Mahazar pertaining to Niranjan Singh S/o Nagarajsingh which is not concerned to this case.
15. Ex.P11 is the copy of the Motor Vehicle Accident Report dated 11.1.2022 in which damage noticed by Motor Vehicle Inspector in the car No. AP-09-BG-9749 and Canter No. AP-39-W-6438 are mentioned.

In the police records name of Dhanranesh is noted as inmates of the car No.
AP-09-BG-9749 which was standing stationary car and victim of the accident.
16. In this case the respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioners regarding the reason, mode and consequence of the accident .

Rajamma.C vs Ronuri Ramakrishna on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126417555/
3 17.

Hence, I have concluded that on 08.01.2022 at 05.00 AM, when Dharanesh and others are standing beside stationary car No.AP-09-BG-9749 between Reddygollahalli cross and Doddapayalagurki cross on NH-44 within the limits of Peresandra Police Station, Gudibande Taluk,
Srinivasachari S/o Venkatachari negligently drive the canter No. AP-39-W-6438 dashed the same to Dharanesh and thereby caused the accident caused death of Dhanranesh.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

In the evidence PW.1 stated that as on the date of accident her son Dhanranesh being graduate use to earn Rs.20,000/- per month by working as Coolie and used to contribute entire income to the family.
In the evidence PW.1 produced SSLC Marks card, PUC Marks card, Study Certificate of Dharanesh.
In the cross- examination PW.1 stated that Dharanesh was going to college apart from doing coolie work.
PW.1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of accident, her son was aged 24 years.
19. In the Adhar card marked at Ex.P7 date of birth of Dhanranesh is noted 01.01.1999.
In the SSLC Marks Card marked at Ex.P12 date of birth of Dharanesh is noted as 19.08.2001.
Copies of the Adhar cards shows that petitioners are parents of Dharanesh.
In the file there are no documents regarding the income and occupation of Dharanesh.

Hence, I have calculated the loss of dependency in the following terms:
Sl. Particulars Amount in No. Rs.
a) Age of the deceased as on the date of accident 21 or 23 years b) Notional income of the deceased as on 15,000/-
 the date of accident  c) 50% addition 7,500/-
 d) 50% deduction towards personal 11,250/-
 expenses  e) Balance 11,250/-
 f) 11,250/- x 12 x 18 = 24,30,000/-
Hence, I award Rs.24,30,000/- towards loss of dependency, Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate,
Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.88,000/-
(44,000 x 2) towards loss of consortium.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioners being parents of Dharanesh are entitle Rs.25,51,000/- with current and future interest @ 6% p.a., as Rajamma.C vs Ronuri Ramakrishna on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126417555/
4 compensation from the respondents.
20. In the written statement respondent No.2 insurance company admitted subsistence of the policy with respect to canter No. AP-39-W-6438 as on the date of accident.
In the file there are no evidence to show as on the date of accident respondent No.1 owner of the canter has violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being owner and insurer of the canter No.AP-39-W-6438 are liable to pay compensation and an award is passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Hence, I answer Issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act by the petitioners, the parents of Dhanranesh is hereby partly allowed.

The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.25,51,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lakhs Fifty one Thousand only) with current and future interest @ 6% p.a., to the petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.2 being insurer of the Canter No. AP-39-W-6438 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within three months from today.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioners equally.
After deposit of the compensation amount 50% of compensation and interest may be released to the petitioners by crediting the same to their bank account directly.
Surplus compensation amount and interest shall be deposited in any bank in the name of the petitioners for a period of two years without permitting to create any encumbrance.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer Gr.I, transcribed by him, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 04th day of October, 2024)

(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
